reason: The fibroblast conditions specify a developmental route from pluripotent cells toward the supporting-tissue lineage.
expectation: A group of stem-cell descendants will develop toward fibroblasts.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch is also a goal, but I can start with the supporting-tissue branch.

effect: The fibroblast branch now has collagen RNA messages, while the unspecialized population remains available for the muscle branch.
reaction: The connection between unchanged DNA and selective collagen gene expression is clear.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to translate the collagen messages into protein.
expectation: The fibroblast-lineage cells will use the amino acids to make collagen protein.

alternatives.reason: The separate muscle branch can also be started now.

effect: The fibroblasts now produce procollagen in secretory vesicles, suggesting an extracellular step remains.
reaction: The ER-to-Golgi connection makes collagen production more concrete.
reason: Extracellular fluid contains processing enzymes and space outside cells, making it a plausible next step for secreted procollagen.
expectation: The fibroblasts will secrete procollagen for extracellular processing into supporting material.

alternatives.reason: I could start the muscle branch instead.

effect: The fibroblasts have secreted and assembled collagen into extracellular matrix; living supporting tissue may require combining that matrix with the cells.
reaction: The distinction between intracellular production and extracellular assembly is useful.
reason: Supporting tissue consists of living cells together with their extracellular matrix, so combining these is a plausible next step.
expectation: The fibroblasts and collagen-rich matrix will form a living supporting tissue.

alternatives.reason: I could start the separate muscle-forming branch first.

effect: The fibroblasts and matrix formed living supporting tissue, completing that goal; the muscle branch remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the cells and their extracellular material come together as tissue.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions specify a route from the remaining unspecialized cells to muscle progenitors.
expectation: The stem-cell descendants will develop into muscle-forming progenitors.

effect: The muscle branch now has committed cells with muscle-protein RNA messages, but no mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between committed cells and mature muscle is clear.
reason: As with the collagen branch, amino acids can supply the building blocks for proteins specified by the new messages.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to make muscle proteins and advance toward muscle formation.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells became separate myoblasts containing muscle proteins, completing the goal without yet forming mature fibres.
reaction: The contrast between prepared myoblasts and a fused muscle fibre is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue was most worthwhile: the sequence connected collagen gene expression and protein production to extracellular assembly, then showed cells and matrix together as tissue.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle branch repeated the familiar messages-plus-amino-acids pattern, although the comparison between lineages gave that repetition a purpose.

surprise.text: The collagen was assembled outside the fibroblasts after procollagen production inside them; that separation made the origin of extracellular matrix clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining the matrix with fibroblasts was a slightly artificial extra step after the picture had already shown the living cells beside their material.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the separate myoblasts develop into mature fibres, especially since this chapter deliberately stops before fusion.
